title: Contact-Aware Gear: neural-operator surrogate for spur-gear tooth stress under quasi-static frictional contact (code, datasets, trained models and result logs)
description:
Code, processed finite-element datasets, trained model checkpoints and result logs for a ten-member Fourier Neural Operator surrogate of the in-plane stress field in a spur-gear tooth under quasi-static frictional contact.

Version 3.0.0 uses a corrected gear-mesh finite-element model: conjugate tooth placement, a normal approach along the line of action with a tangential slip in the direction of the kinematic sliding, and no initial contact-node adjustment. Trained on 432 CalculiX solutions and tested on three held-out loading trajectories, the ensemble reproduces the finite-element field with a relative L2 error of 1.4% (R2 = 0.9999) and the peak root tensile stress to 1.0%, and follows the change of the field with the friction coefficient case by case. Refining every mesh length scale 1.5-fold changes the labels by 9.0% and leaves the surrogate 8.9% from the refined solution. The finite-element contact agrees with Hertz theory to within 9%. One prediction takes 76 ms on a CPU against 27.1 s for a CalculiX solve.

This deposit contains the gearstress package; 61 dataset-generation, training, study, analysis and figure scripts; the test suite; the model-ready HDF5 datasets, including the corrected datasets v4 and v4f and the earlier datasets v1 to v3 used for method comparisons; every gear-mesh solution on the prediction grid with its refined references; 40 trained checkpoints, 20 behind the headline results and 20 on the earlier dataset v2; and the per-seed result logs and study summaries. The remaining checkpoints of the earlier datasets and the raw CalculiX output are available on reasonable request.

Source code is released under the MIT License; datasets, result logs and trained checkpoints under CC BY 4.0.
